To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the extent of genetic related between training and testing sets has an important effect on predictive ability, and that the relationship structure of the training set is important for low heritability, but not for high heritability, traits.
the accuracy of whole genome prediction depends on the genetic relatedness between the training and testing sets, but that the relationship is not straightforward.
The extent of genetic related-ness across the training and validation sets has an impact on accuracy of whole-genomics predictions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of the extent of genetic related-ness between the training and testing sets of animals on the accuracy of genome-enabled prediction.

the development of new methods and software for the estimation of the accuracy of genome-enabled breeding values, and the application of these methods to the analysis of real data from dairy cattle populations.
the impact of extent of relatedness and the choice of cross-validation layout on the accuracy of genome-enabled prediction in dairy cattle.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the accuracy of genome-enabled predictive ability is affected by the extent of genetic related-ness between training and testing sets, which is not necessarily reflected by the average genetic relationships across the two sets, and that this effect is not uniform for all traits.
, in the case of high heritability, accuracy is mainly affected by the extent of genetic related between the training and testing sets, and the RAN design is recommended.
there is no best CV design for all situations, and that the choice of CV strategy should be based on the purpose of the prediction and the genetic architecture of the trait of interest
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CV layout should be designed to resemble the actual use of the predictive model.
the choice of CV layout should depend on the intended application of the predictions and on the heritable nature of the traits.

the CV design is a critical aspect of whole-genome prediction and that it should be considered in the same way that the choice of training and testing animals for a traditional pedigree-based evaluation would be considered, with an emphasis on ensuring that the CV layout is appropriate for the intended application.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CV strategies should not only be chosen based on their statistical properties but also on their relevance to the intended use of predictive models.

the accuracy of genomic predictions is not only a function of the amount of information in the training set but also of the genetic relationships between the training and testing sets, which is determined by the CV design.
, when estimating the predictive ability of genomic models, it is important to ensure that the training and testing sets have similar relationships to the intended use of predictions.
